title: What hisbonenus is: iyun, the depth of the concept, and daas
overview:
The book opens by asking what *hisbonenus* is. It is *iyun*, the inner side of *bina*: staying on a concept, cutting it into all its parts, until one reaches its depth, as against *girsa*, a passing glance. What the world calls concentration is only a *kli*. It gives no content, and taking it for the thing itself is "the whole mistake of idol worship". The depth of a concept in *bina* is only its *tamtzis*, like instant coffee, yet it is the fiftieth gate. Delving into it reaches the hidden *chachma*, the aquifer under every spring, and brings new light into the same book.

Innovation comes only within a field, from the people who know every part of the motor, never from going for *chiddushim*. The *navon*, like the Wright brothers with their bicycle chain, carries an idea from one field to another. The text runs from depth to length; the student goes the other way, one length at a time. *Daas* is the dive, not the floor of the ocean: it squeezes the whole mind onto one point, and *daas* and *bina* depend on each other.

sections.title: Hisbonenus is iyun, a long look, and not girsa, a passing glance
sections.summary: The chapter sets out to say what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is in itself: a strong gaze into the depth of a matter, staying with it until it is understood in every detail. This is the inner side of *bina*, the *iyun* of the Talmud, as against *girsa*, which takes a thing in at first glance and soon forgets it.

phrases.he: הנה כבר מבואר באריכות בקונטרס מיוחד
phrases.en: It has already been explained at length in a special tract

phrases.he: בפרטי אופני ההתפעלות במוח ולב,
phrases.en: on the particular ways of *hispaalus* (arousal) in the mind and the heart,

phrases.he: ומחשבה שנולד מן ההתבוננות
phrases.en: and of the thought that is born of *hisbonenus* (contemplation),

phrases.he: לפי סדר ה' מדריגות נפש רוח נשמה חיה יחידה כו'.
phrases.en: according to the order of the five levels, *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*, *chaya* and *yechida*.

phrases.he: ומעתה יש לבאר היטב במהות גוף ענין ההתבוננות,
phrases.en: Now we must explain well what *hisbonenus* itself is:

phrases.he: מה היא בעצם ובמה יתבונן.
phrases.en: what it is essentially, and on what one should contemplate.

phrases.he: והנה מהות ההתבוננות בעצם הוא ענין ההסתכלות החזקה בעמקות הענין
phrases.en: What *hisbonenus* is, essentially, is a strong gazing into the depth of the matter,

phrases.he: ולעמוד עליו הרבה
phrases.en: staying on it a long time,

phrases.he: עד שיבין אותו על בוריו בכל חלקיו בפרטי פרטיות
phrases.en: until one understands it clearly, in all its parts, down to the finest details.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת פנימיות בינה
phrases.en: It is the inner aspect of *bina*,

phrases.he: הנקרא בלשון הגמרא בשם עיון,
phrases.en: which in the language of the Gemara is called *iyun* (close analysis),

phrases.he: כמו שאמר במסכת סוכה הא למגרס והא לעיוני
phrases.en: as it says in tractate Sukka: "This one is for *girsa* (reading through), and this one for *iyun*."

phrases.he: פירוש הגירסא הוא רק הבנת הדבר בהשקפה ראשונה,
phrases.en: *Girsa* means understanding the thing only at first glance,

phrases.he: שהולכת ונובעת במהירות בלתי עכוב והעמדה כלל כידוע
phrases.en: which goes and flows quickly, without holding back or stopping at all, as is known.

phrases.he: על דרך משל המביט בעינו על דבר מה
phrases.en: For example, one who looks at something with his eye

phrases.he: ואינו מתבונן כלל על הדבר באיכותו ומהותו בכל חלקיו הפנימים וחיצונים,
phrases.en: and does not consider at all what kind of thing it is and what it is, in all its inner and outer parts,

phrases.he: רק דרך מעביר בעלמא
phrases.en: but only in passing:

phrases.he: שבמשך זמן ודאי ישכח עליו לגמרי
phrases.en: in time he will surely forget it completely,

phrases.he: וגם לא יוכל לספר לזולתו רק כלליות ענין אותו הדבר שראה
phrases.en: and he will be able to tell another only the general outline of the thing he saw,

phrases.he: בהעברת העין ולא בטביעת עין כלל
phrases.en: with a passing eye, and not with a fixed look at all.

phrases.he: וכן העברת עין השכל באיזה סברא בהשקפה ראשונה
phrases.en: So too when the mind's eye passes over some *sevara* (line of reasoning) at first glance,

phrases.he: בלתי עכוב והעמדה לעיין בו היטב,
phrases.en: without holding back and stopping to look into it well:

phrases.he: ולא ידע בסברא זו לתכליתה כלל
phrases.en: he will not know this *sevara* to its end at all.

sections.title: Width, length and depth: a concept is like a river, and iyun goes to its depth
sections.summary: Every concept has width (its explanation to every side), length (its descent into *meshalim*, down to a child) and depth (its essential point, like the current of a river, from which all the rest spreads). *Iyun* stays on a concept, slowly, to reach that depth; that is *hisbonenus*, with the doubled *nun*.

phrases.he: כי הנה ג' דברים הוא שיש בכל דבר מושכל.
phrases.en: For there are three things in every concept:

phrases.he: עומק ואורך ורוחב.
phrases.en: depth, length and width.

phrases.he: הרוחב הוא בחינת הסבר המושכל לכל צד בפרטים הרבה
phrases.en: The width is the explanation of the concept to every side, in many details,

phrases.he: כרוחב הנהר,
phrases.en: like the width of a river;

phrases.he: ולא דברים כהווייתן לבד, כנהר קצר.
phrases.en: and not only things as they are, like a narrow river.

phrases.he: ואורך הוא עוצם ירידות ההשכלה להלביש את המושכל במשלים שונים
phrases.en: The length is the great descent of the idea, dressing the concept in different *meshalim* (analogies)

phrases.he: עד להביאו בהשגות התינוק קטן כו',
phrases.en: until it is brought within a small child's grasp,

phrases.he: כנהר שהולך ומתמשך לאורך
phrases.en: like a river that goes on and stretches out in length

phrases.he: (וכמו שמבואר באריכות בכתבים בענין אורך היריעה כו')
phrases.en: (as is explained at length in the writings about the length of the curtain).

phrases.he: והעומק הוא כעומק הנהר
phrases.en: The depth is like the depth of a river,

phrases.he: שמשם מתרחב ובעצמו אינו רחב כלל,
phrases.en: from which it widens, though in itself it is not wide at all;

phrases.he: אבל הוא עיקר עצם הנהר (הנקרא שטרוים)
phrases.en: but it is the main body of the river (called the current),

phrases.he: שהוא עיקר מרוצת הילוכו ממקורו
phrases.en: the main force of its flow from its source.

phrases.he: ומים שעל גביו בגובה ולצדדי העומק טפלים אליו,
phrases.en: The water above it, in height and to the sides of the depth, is secondary to it;

phrases.he: שאינן רק בחינת התגברות התפשטותו בלבד, לצדדים ברוחב ובגובה ובאורך ההילוך כו'
phrases.en: it is only the force of its spreading out, to the sides in width, in height, and in the length of its course.

phrases.he: כך עומק המושכל הוא בחינת עצם נקודתו כמו שהוא,
phrases.en: So the depth of a concept is its very point, as it is,

phrases.he: ונקרא עומק המושג
phrases.en: and it is called *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept).

phrases.he: שכל מה שנתפשט בהסבר ההשגה לכל צד,
phrases.en: For all that spreads out in the explanation of the comprehension to every side,

phrases.he: ברוחב גדול בכמה פרטים,
phrases.en: in great width, in many details,

phrases.he: וכן לאורך בעוצם הירידה,
phrases.en: and also in length, in the great descent,

phrases.he: וגם בחינת הגובה למעלה, להשכיל ממנו עוד למעלה ממנו הרבה,
phrases.en: and also the height above, to understand from it much higher still

phrases.he: (עד בחינת עומק רום כמו התגברות המים למעלה מעלה בזמן המבול
phrases.en: (up to the depth of the height, like the waters rising higher and higher at the time of the Flood;

phrases.he: שכזה יהיה לימות המשיח ברוחניות בשנת ת"ר לחיי נח
phrases.en: so will it be in the days of Moshiach, spiritually, in the six hundredth year of Noach's life,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזוהר דאתפתחו מבועין דחכמתא כו'
phrases.en: as it says in the *Zohar*, "the fountains of wisdom were opened":

phrases.he: והיינו מעיינות תהום החכמה שיתגברו למעלה מעלה ויכסו כל ההרים כו'
phrases.en: that is, the springs of the deep of wisdom, which will rise higher and higher and cover all the mountains;

phrases.he: וארובות השמים נפתחו כו'
phrases.en: and "the windows of heaven were opened,"

phrases.he: להמשיך מן המים שמעל השמים
phrases.en: to draw from the waters above the heavens,

phrases.he: הנקרא עומק רום שתלוי בעומק תחת
phrases.en: which is called the depth of the height, and depends on the depth below,

phrases.he: כי נעוץ תחילתן בסופן
phrases.en: for their beginning is fixed in their end,

phrases.he: כמו העמק שאלה או הגבה למעלה כו'
phrases.en: as in "ask it in the depth, or in the height above";

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בכתבים)
phrases.en: and as is written in the writings)

phrases.he: הכל נמשך מעצם עומק נקודתו כמו שהוא נובע מן החכמה הנקרא אין,
phrases.en: all of it is drawn from the very depth of its point, as it flows from *chachma*, which is called *ayin* (nothing);

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב ונהר יוצא מעדן כו'
phrases.en: as it is written, "And a river goes out from Eden":

phrases.he: שהבינה נקרא נהר והחכמה נקרא מעיין, כידוע
phrases.en: for *bina* is called a river, and *chachma* a spring, as is known.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא עיון,
phrases.en: This is what is called *iyun*:

phrases.he: שעומד על דבר המושכל ומעיין בו הרבה מאד,
phrases.en: one stays on the concept and looks into it very much;

phrases.he: שהוא העיכוב היפך המהירות
phrases.en: it is a holding back, the opposite of speed,

phrases.he: דהיינו כדי לבא לעומקו של המושכל
phrases.en: that is, in order to come to the depth of the concept

phrases.he: כמו שהוא בעצם פנימיותו ותוך תוכו דווקא
phrases.en: as it is in its very inwardness and innermost core, *davka*;

phrases.he: כמו המסתכל על דבר מה בעינו ולא בהעברה בעלמא,
phrases.en: like one who looks at something with his eye, not merely in passing,

phrases.he: אלא בפקוח וטביעת עינו בעיכוב גדול,
phrases.en: but with open eyes and a fixed look, holding back a long time,

phrases.he: עד שיודע אותו היטב בכל חלקיו הפנימים ותוך תוכו כו'
phrases.en: until he knows it well in all its inner parts and its innermost core.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא התבוננות בנו''ן הכפול דוקא,
phrases.en: This is what is called *hisbonenus*, with the doubled *nun*, *davka*:

phrases.he: דהיינו שמתבונן ומעיין בו הרבה
phrases.en: that is, he contemplates it and looks into it a great deal;

phrases.he: וכמו שפירש רש''י: בעיוני, לעמוד על הדבר להבינו על בוריו כו'.
phrases.en: as Rashi explained, "for *iyun*: to stand on the thing, to understand it clearly."

sections.title: Concentration is only a vessel; delving reaches the aquifer of chachma
sections.summary: What the world calls concentration, *ha'amakas hadaas*, is only a *kli*: it supplies no content, and taking it for the thing itself is the mistake of idol worship. Delving, *ma'amik*, goes past the explanation to the root of a concept, *taalumos chachma*, the one aquifer that every spring of wisdom comes from.

phrases.he: ונמצא בחינת העיון הזה הוא רק בחינת כלי לבחינת ההעמקה דבינה עצמה,
phrases.en: So this *iyun* is only a *kli* (vessel) for the depth of *bina* itself.

phrases.he: כי לכאורה בחינת העיון הזה נקרא העמקת הדעת בלשון בעולם,
phrases.en: For at first glance this *iyun* is what people call *ha'amakas hadaas* (concentration), in the language of the world,

phrases.he: ואינו כן,
phrases.en: but it is not so:

phrases.he: דהעמקת הדעת היינו בחינת כלי לבד לבוא לעומק של הענין ממש
phrases.en: concentration is only a *kli* for coming to the depth of the matter itself, *mamash*.

blocks.text:
**So this *iyun* is only a *kli* (vessel) for the depth of *bina* itself.** That is what has been said until now: the *iyun*, which is *bina sheb'bina*, is a *kli* for the *hasaga* (comprehension), which is the *omek hamusag*, the *Keser* of *bina*. The learning is the *kli* for understanding the explanation.

The text doesn't say it here, but the chain goes on. The *hasaga* is a *kli* for the *havana*, the outer *chachma*: to actually see the thing, not just the explanation. *Hasaga* means to understand the explanation; *havana* means to see the thing. The *havana* is the *kli* for *taalumos chachma* (the hidden parts of *chachma*), to really see the inner essence of the thing. That is already a knowing, a *daas*, but the *daas elyon* (higher knowledge) of *Keser*. And that is the *kli* for *Radla*: to experience the thing itself, without anything of yourself at all; "does not know" means you have no self-concept in it. And so it goes on and on: each lower level is a *kli* for a higher one. But now he is going to go down a little, instead of up.

Now the text goes down. **For at first glance this *iyun* is what people call *ha'amakas hadaas* (concentration)**. This business of *iyun* is what everybody calls contemplation or meditation. You notice that the book says *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*, and they call it the tract of meditation, or contemplation. That is what people call it, in the language of the world, **but it is not so**. The concentration is also a *kli*, to hold all these other things.

At each level the *daas* is the outer *kli*. On the level of *bina sheb'bina*, if you don't have concentration, the *bina sheb'bina* won't work. On the next level up, going from the *omek hamusag* to the actual *haskala* of the thing, you also need *daas*; and to go from the *havana* of *chachma* to the inner *chachma*, you also need *daas*. Once you know the explanation, you have to concentrate on that explanation in order to go to the next, deeper level. So the *daas* is a *kli* to go deeper and deeper into it, but it is not the depth itself. It is an instrument.

The *bina sheb'bina* is also not the thing itself; it is also an instrument. But the *daas* is not even that kind of an instrument. The *daas* is an instrument for an instrument, because the *bina sheb'bina*, which is on the explanation, is what will actually get you there.

And this is basically the whole mistake of idol worship. As a matter of fact, that is what idol worship is: they see the *daas* as the primary instrument. They might even understand that of course the concentration is not the thing itself, that the thing is "the G-d realization, or whatever they want to call it". But they arrive at it directly from the *daas*: you concentrate, you think "G-d, G-d, G-d" or something like that, and the concentration will get you there.

sensitivity.reason: Calls practices that seek G-d through concentration alone idol worship.
sensitivity.publishable: This is the mistake of approaches that make concentration the primary instrument. They may understand that the concentration is not the thing itself, "the G-d realization, or whatever they want to call it". But they try to arrive at it directly from the *daas*: you concentrate, you think "G-d, G-d, G-d" or something like that, and the concentration is supposed to get you there.

blocks.text: But what he is saying is that the *daas* is a *kli*, not to reach the matter, only to go deeper into the matter. You already have to have the matter to start off with. The basic thing is that the *daas* has to have content, and the *daas* by itself does not supply the content. It is the *bina sheb'bina* that supplies the content.

phrases.he: ולמעלה מזה הוא נקרא מעמיק,
phrases.en: Above this is what is called *ma'amik* (delving),

phrases.he: שמגיע למעלה גם מן החכמה עצמה,
phrases.en: which reaches higher even than *chachma* itself,

blocks.text:
**Above this is what is called *ma'amik* (delving)**. *Ma'amik* is also concentration; it is all the same thing. When it is on the *bina sheb'bina*, that is the lower one, *ha'amakas hadaas*. *Ma'amik* is when you are concentrating on the *omek hamusag*, even when you have it by way of a *mashal*: you keep concentrating and thinking it over and over, and this **reaches higher even than *chachma* itself**.

It gets you past a general overview. The outer *chachma* means you get the explanation in a way of seeing. You don't just see the explanation, you see what the explanation is about; but you don't see *mamash* what the actual thing is about. That is *taalumos chachma*, and it can be higher still. Once you are in *taalumos chachma* you can even see what some other things are about, because it gets to the root of the thing. Not just the thing: the actual root of the thing.

blocks.title: The physicist and the root of physics
blocks.text: Take physics. There is the explanation. Then there is the real physicist, who already has it in a way that he understands more than just the explanation. That doesn't mean he has the actual root of the physics, which is something like metaphysics. That is already the root of the physics, and the root of the physics will answer questions in other fields too. That is *taalumos chachma*.

phrases.he: שהגם שהחכמה היא בחינת האין ממש של המושכל,
phrases.en: For although *chachma* is the very *ayin* (nothing) of the concept,

phrases.he: קודם שבא לכלל עומק נקודת המושג שבבינה,
phrases.en: before it comes into the depth of the point of the concept in *bina*,

phrases.he: כמעיין לגבי נהר כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like a spring compared to a river, as said above,

phrases.he: אבל בחינת העמקה בשרש של המושכל,
phrases.en: still, delving into the root of the concept:

phrases.he: שרשה מגיע בשרש הממשיך לנביעת מעיין דחכמה כו',
phrases.en: its root reaches into the root that draws forth the flow of the spring of *chachma*,

phrases.he: ונקרא עמקי החכמה או תעלומות חכמה,
phrases.en: and it is called the depths of *chachma*, or *taalumos chachma*;

phrases.he: כי כמו שיש עומק ואורך ורוחב בבינה שנקרא יש כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: for just as there is depth, length and width in *bina*, which is called *yesh* (something), as said above,

phrases.he: כך יש עומק ואורך ורוחב במעיין דחכמה שנקרא אין
phrases.en: so there is depth, length and width in the spring of *chachma*, which is called *ayin*.

blocks.text: **For although *chachma* is the very *ayin* (nothing) of the concept**: *chachma* is when the concept is still not in a particular way or a particular explanation, and the *omek hamusag* is the depth *davka* according to this particular explanation. So *chachma* is an *ayin* compared to the depth of the point of the concept in *bina*, like a spring compared to a river. But delving into the root of the concept reaches **the root that draws forth the flow of the spring of *chachma***.

A scientist can look deeply into physics or something like that and get all kinds of insights, but he won't look even deeper: how did the whole thing come into existence in the first place? Yes, there are laws. And this is the thing: they are missing it even in their own language. They say "the laws of nature". A law, by the very word they use, means somebody is making this law. Where does this law come from? In other words, what is the root of the *muskal* (the concept)?

sensitivity.reason: A jab at scientists for missing the point in their own language.
sensitivity.publishable: A scientist can look deeply into physics and get all kinds of insights, but the deeper question is how the whole thing came into existence in the first place. Even the language says it: "the laws of nature". A law means somebody is making this law. Where does this law come from? In other words, what is the root of the *muskal* (the concept)?

blocks.text: If you don't keep thinking more about the root of the *muskal*, you can get as far as the *ayin*, where you understand the *chachma* not in a way of an explanation, and you didn't think about it any further. But delving into the root reaches the root that draws forth the spring of *chachma*: that is where the whole spring of *chachma* comes from. So **it is called the depths of *chachma*, or *taalumos chachma***: the hidden parts of *chachma*. Just as *bina*, called *yesh*, has depth, length and width, so does the spring of *chachma*, called *ayin*.

phrases.he: ועומק המעיין היינו תחילת שרש מחצבו בעומקו,
phrases.en: The depth of the spring is the beginning of the root of its source, in its depth,

phrases.he: שמשם מתפשט נביעתו למעלה עד שבוקע ויוצא טיפין טיפין בגילוי מהעלמו,
phrases.en: from which its flow spreads upward until it breaks through and comes out drop by drop, revealed, from its hiddenness;

phrases.he: ותכלית העלמו הוא תכלית עמקו למטה,
phrases.en: and the utmost of its hiddenness is the utmost of its depth, below,

phrases.he: כמו מעיינות תהום נבקעו,
phrases.en: as in "the wellsprings of the deep burst open":

phrases.he: דארעא חלחולי מחלחלא כו'
phrases.en: for the earth is full of fissures,

phrases.he: בגידין שיש להם עומק ראשון,
phrases.en: in veins that have a first depth.

phrases.he: ובזה נאמר והחכמה מאין,
phrases.en: About this it is said, "*Chachma* is [found] from *ayin*":

phrases.he: מהעלם החכמה הנקרא עומק החכמה
phrases.en: from the hiddenness of *chachma*, which is called the depth of *chachma*.

blocks.title: One aquifer under Pittsburgh and California
blocks.text: **The depth of the spring is the beginning of the root of its source, in its depth**. Under the ground there is what is called the aquifer: like a giant ocean under the ground that the spring comes from. You'll see one spring and you'll see another spring, and really they both connect to the same *taalumos chachma*. If you follow physics, or if you follow psychology, to their ultimate conclusion, they really come from the same source. On the surface it's two different things: this one is in Pittsburgh, that one is in California. But when you go down far enough, you see there's really one big ocean down there that they're both coming from.

**comes out drop by drop, revealed, from its hiddenness**: that is the external spring. **as in "the wellsprings of the deep burst open"**: what we call the spring is really the tail of the spring. It's not the actual spring, just the end of it; it is like the *Malchus* of the spring, not the *Keser* of the spring. The earth has veins in it, fissures, and these veins run through all kinds of things, the same as with oil. **in veins that have a first depth**: these springs you see out here are not the real *mahus* (what it is in itself) of the spring. What really makes the spring is the first depth, the aquifer. **About this it is said, "*Chachma* is [found] from *ayin*"**: from the hiddenness of *chachma*, which is called the depth of *chachma*.

phrases.he: והחכמה הוא המצאת שכל החדש שיוצא כברק
phrases.en: *Chachma* is the discovery of a new idea, which comes out like lightning,

phrases.he: כו' כידוע,
phrases.en: as is known;

phrases.he: ומקור מחצבו בהעלם עומקו הוא עיקר עצמיות ותוך תוכו
phrases.en: but the source of its origin, in the hiddenness of its depth, is the main thing: its selfness and its innermost core.

blocks.text:
"*Chachma* is found from *ayin*" means that the *chachma* is already a *metzius* (an existence), and the real *ayin* of *chachma* is *taalumos chachma*. And what is *chachma*? Now he gives the definition: **the discovery of a new idea, which comes out like lightning**, a lightning bolt.

But this lightning is really *Yesod Abba* already. When it comes out as a flash, that is already the *yesh* of the *chachma*, even in revealed *chachma*. *Yesod* is already the connection to the outside: the flash is where you can bring the idea into an actual *yesh*, and when somebody has a new thought, the *bina* brings it out from this flash. In another place it explains that this is called *Yesod Abba*: it is coming out.

So he is saying two things here: it is the discovery of a new idea that comes out like lightning, **but the source of its origin, in the hiddenness of its depth**, is the real selfness of the *chachma*. The real thing of *chachma* is *taalumos chachma*, in the *Keser*.

That is why in a lot of the Kabbalistic and Chassidic books, sometimes it says *chachma* and means revealed *chachma*, and a lot of times it says *chachma* and really means the *chachma* of *Arich*. As a matter of fact, when it says that the Torah comes from *chachma*, it really means from the *chachma* of *Arich*, not from the revealed *chachma* of *Atzilus*.

sections.title: The depth of the concept is a tamtzis, and yet it is the fiftieth gate
sections.summary: The depth of the concept in *bina* is only the *tamtzis* of an explanation, the *ayin* of its *yesh*, like instant coffee from the beans. Yet it is the *shaar hanun*, whose root reaches the depths of *chachma*: delving into it brings new light into the same book, and, unlike a bare flash, holds that light as a *yesh* that can be explained.

phrases.he: כנ"ל בביאור ענין עומק המושג דבינה
phrases.en: As explained above about the depth of the concept in *bina*:

phrases.he: שאינ' רק העומק של ההשגה דבינה
phrases.en: it is only the depth of the comprehension of *bina*,

phrases.he: המורגש בבחינת יש בהבנת דבר מה בסברא נגלית,
phrases.en: felt as a *yesh*, when one understands something in a revealed *sevara*;

phrases.he: שעומק של הסבר ההשגה הוא בחינת אין של היש דהשגה בלבד,
phrases.en: the depth of the explanation of the comprehension is only the *ayin* of the *yesh* of the comprehension,

phrases.he: ואין לו ערך לגבי אין דחכמה טרם שבא לכלל השגה כלל,
phrases.en: and it has no comparison to the *ayin* of *chachma* before it comes into comprehension at all,

phrases.he: גם לא בבחינת העומק שבה,
phrases.en: not even to the depth that is in it,

phrases.he: שהוא תמציתה
phrases.en: which is its *tamtzis* (essence).

blocks.text: Now he uses the *bina* as a *mashal* for the *chachma*. **As explained above about the depth of the concept in *bina***: the *omek hamusag* is the depth of the explanation, felt in an actual way of a somethingness, when you understand something in a revealed *sevara*. A *sevara* means a particular *sevara*; a *sevara* is already a *yesh*, like a theory. When you understand the explanation, it is in a way of an *ayin*, but it is only the *ayin* of the *yesh* of this explanation. **and it has no comparison to the *ayin* of *chachma* before it comes into comprehension at all**, where the *chachma* is still not in this particular explanation altogether.

Remember, now he is not really explaining *bina*; he is explaining *chachma*, and the *bina* is a *mashal* for it. Here he tells you that the *omek hamusag* is the *ayin* of the *yesh*. And over there, the flash is the *yesh* of the *ayin*. There is a deeper *ayin* of the *ayin*, and even deeper than that, the *ayin* in *taalumos chachma*, the total *ayin*, which has nothing to do with this particular *chachma* altogether. All the wisdoms come from it. It's not just this spring that comes from it; all the springs come from it.

**which is its *tamtzis* (essence)**: this *omek hamusag* is the *tamtzis*. A *tamtzis* means the essence, like essence of almond. (By the way, in English somehow they use "essence" for self.) That is why one has to ask why he uses *davka* this term here. A *tamtzis* is usually the essence that is a derivative, after you've already processed the thing and come to the ultimate conclusion after the process. That is the *omek hamusag*: after you process the whole explanation you come to its *tamtzis*, and now you understand, like addition.

blocks.question: So how do you translate *Atzmus*?
blocks.text: *Atzmus* is selfness. It is always mistranslated: they call it "quintessential" and stuff like that, and it's really a very bad mistranslation. Essence means *tamtzis*, and a *tamtzis* means that you processed the whole thing and got the taste out of it.

blocks.title: Instant coffee, and knowing how to add
blocks.text: Instant coffee is the *tamtzis* of coffee beans: you got out just the part you need. Or take addition. They sit down with little kids and tell them, one fishy plus one fishy is two fishies, and after a while they understand. By the time they get to second or third grade they don't have to learn like that: one plus one is two, then all kinds of things to add, a whole bunch of examples, and you do your homework. Finally, I know how to add. Which example do I know how to add? All of them. But how do I know all of them? Do I have a fantastic computer in my brain with every single addition in it, like 2,500 plus 7,600? No. I just have the *tamtzis* of the whole thing. I threw away all the parts I don't need, all the examples I had to sit and do, and I just have the *tamtzis* of how to add. And that *tamtzis* is just the *omek hamusag*: when you went through the whole explanation, then you have the *tamtzis*.

blocks.title: "She thinks there's a G-d in the world; I know it"
blocks.text:
It explains in other places (as a matter of fact, he thinks it's in *Kuntres HaHispaalus*) that there's a summary before the *hisbonenus* and a summary after the *hisbonenus*. The summary before the *hisbonenus* is: there's a G-d in the world.

Like the story told about the Deitschel, though some people say it was the Alter Rebbe with his father-in-law. He was asked, "So what did you learn?" He said, "I learned there's a G-d in the world." "Hey, the maid knows that." And he called the maid: "Do you know there's a G-d in the world?" She says, "Sure, who does not know there's a G-d in the world?" So he answered: "She thinks there's a G-d in the world. I know there's a G-d in the world."

He had the summary after the *hisbonenus*, and she had the summary before the *hisbonenus*. And here is another point where they make their mistake: the summary before and the summary after look exactly the same, on the surface. He said exactly what the maid said: "I know there's a G-d in the world." So what's the difference? What makes him the big Rebbe, and she's just a stupid maid? Because he had the *tamtzis* afterwards. And not only that: as he is going to explain, even the *tamtzis* isn't the end. There's more after the *tamtzis*. So that is the *omek hamusag*.

phrases.he: ואמנם עומק המושג נקרא שער הנו''ן דבינה,
phrases.en: However, the depth of the concept is called the *shaar hanun* (fiftieth gate) of *bina*;

phrases.he: גם שנמשך מאין דחכמה ליש,
phrases.en: even though it is drawn from the *ayin* of *chachma* to a *yesh*

phrases.he: (כמו מעיין יוצא מבית קדש הקדשים תחלתו כקרני חגבים
phrases.en: (like the spring that comes out of the Holy of Holies: at its start it is like the antennae of locusts,

phrases.he: כו' וכהאי גוונא)
phrases.en: and the like),

phrases.he: שרשו מגיע בעומק דחכמה הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: its root reaches into the depth of *chachma* mentioned above.

phrases.he: וכנראה בחוש שכל מעמיק רק בעומק המושג,
phrases.en: And we see it plainly: whoever delves just into the depth of the concept

phrases.he: הוא ממציא למקור ושרש המושכל,
phrases.en: finds the source and root of the concept,

phrases.he: להמציא בחינת חדשות דאור החכמה בבינה,
phrases.en: bringing out new things of the light of *chachma* in *bina*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא מעמיק לשון מפעיל,
phrases.en: This is what is called *ma'amik*, a causative form,

phrases.he: שמפעיל לעומ' דחו"ב
phrases.en: for it activates the depth of *chachma* and *bina*.

blocks.text: **However, the depth of the concept is called the *shaar hanun* (fiftieth gate) of *bina***. "But wait a minute, there's another *omek hamusag*." ("However" here means "but".) In other places the *omek hamusag* of *bina* is called the *shaar hanun* of *bina*. Now, the *shaar hanun* of *bina* is not so simple, because we say that even Moshe Rabbeinu had a hard time getting to the *shaar hanun* of *bina*. So how can it be just the *tamtzis* of the explanation, the depth of *bina*? It says there is depth, and there is depth of the depth.

blocks.title: The locust's antenna, the shofar and the horn of plenty
blocks.text: **even though it is drawn from the *ayin* of *chachma* to a *yesh***: the *shaar hanun* is in *bina*, and it is in a way of bringing from the *ayin* of *chachma* to an actual *yesh* of an explanation, a somethingness. Like the spring that comes out of the Holy of Holies: it starts off like the antenna of a locust. That is also why *bina* is called a shofar: the shofar starts narrow and ends up wide. And the horn of plenty, the cornucopia: it also starts narrow on one side and opens up on the other side.

**its root reaches into the depth of *chachma* mentioned above**. The real depth of *bina* goes further. The first depth is the *Keser* of *bina*, meaning the *Keser* of *bina* of *Atzilus*. But just as *chachma* has a depth, in the *chachma* of *Arich*, there is also a *bina* of *Arich*. And the *shaar hanun* keeps going, even higher than that, to the *bina* of *Atik*, and it really keeps going into *Radla*. And really, as he explains later, "we will rejoice and be glad in You, *mamash*", which in a way is even higher than the *chachma*. This is what he explains about the Leviathan, that the Leviathan can jump from the upper waters to the lower waters, and from the lower waters to the upper waters.

**And we see it plainly: whoever delves just into the depth of the concept** finds the source and root of the concept. We see it right here: we are delving into the explanation of *Shaar HaYichud*, the *omek hamusag*. Here, in these first few chapters, he explains what these concepts are, what *hisbonenus* is; and from chapter 10 onwards he really isn't explaining about G-d, he is explaining how the world came into existence, the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds). Nonetheless it is **bringing out new things of the light of *chachma* in *bina***.

blocks.title: Every time, a whole new book
blocks.text: Looking into the *omek hamusag*, even though you are only concentrating on the *omek hamusag* and on the explanation, nonetheless brings a new light of *chachma* into the *bina*. Like Shimon says a lot of times: each time he reads the book, it's like a whole new book. So what do you mean, a whole new book? It's the same book, with exactly the same letters. The book didn't change; nothing funny happened to it. Because now he sees it in a whole new light of *chachma* in the *bina*. The first time, all he did was learn the explanation; the second time, even though he learned it in a new way, again he just learned the explanation. And some of the things we are already talking about are not even explained in the book. So where did we get them? We got them from the book.

**This is what is called *ma'amik*, a causative form**. *Omek hadaas* (depth of *daas*) means just to concentrate on your first learning: when you're learning it, you concentrate on it. Right now we are doing it with *omek hadaas*, using the power of our concentration on what we are talking about. But later on, after we finish talking, we're going to be walking around thinking about it: what does it really mean? What is the root of this thing? And *ma'amik* is a causative form, activation: **for it activates the depth of *chachma* and *bina***, in *Arich*, then in *Atik*, and even more than that.

He doesn't know if the text says this later, but there is a special thing, an advantage, in *bina* over *chachma*. The *shaar hanun* is in a way of a *yesh*; but when the *shaar hanun* reaches into the depth of the *chachma*, it can bring it out. It grabs it as a *yesh*, so that he can take it out and bring it to other people, and bring it into an explanation. Whereas somebody who just gets a spiritual insight, an intuitive feeling, not only won't be able to explain it to somebody else; he might even lose the idea himself. A few days later it dissipates.

Like people who sometimes get real drunk, or stoned, or something like that, and they have this flash of wisdom, and the next day they don't remember what it was at all. Or the story about Edison and other people: sometimes they would have a flash of *chachma*, and if they wouldn't write it down right away, they would forget it. Not only couldn't they explain it, even to themselves; they would *mamash* lose it. Whereas the *shaar hanun* of *bina* goes just as deep as the depth of *chachma*, but gets it in a way of a *yesh*.

sections.title: Wise in understanding, understanding in wisdom: the inventor and the navon
sections.summary: "Be wise in understanding" is *chachma sheb'bina*: a new insight, but only in the same field, and it comes only through the *iyun* of *bina sheb'bina*, held in the *kli* of *daas*; go for *chiddushim* and you make none. "Understand with wisdom" is *bina sheb'chachma*: the power to explain an insight many ways, and, deeper, the *navon* who understands one thing from another, even a different field, because he has reached the aquifer.

phrases.he: (ולפ"ז מ"ש הבן בחכמה וחכם בבינה
phrases.en: (Accordingly, what is said, "Understand with wisdom, and be wise in understanding,"

phrases.he: שמבואר בכתבים, דהיינו ע''ב דס''ג חכם בבינה,
phrases.en: explained in the writings, that is, *Ayin Beis* of *SaG* is "wise in understanding":

phrases.he: שהוא רק להבין דבר חידוש אחר מתוך המושג דבינה,
phrases.en: it is only to understand another new thing from the concept of *bina* [itself],

phrases.he: שזה אינו אלא על ידי בחינת העיון הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: and this comes only through the *iyun* mentioned above,

phrases.he: שהוא המברר כל חלקיו על בוריו,
phrases.en: which sorts out all its parts clearly,

phrases.he: ונקרא בינה שבבינה
phrases.en: and is called *bina sheb'bina*.

blocks.text: **"Understand with wisdom, and be wise in understanding"**. "Wise in understanding" means *chachma* of *bina*. And what is *chachma* of *bina*? **it is only to understand another new thing from the concept of *bina* [itself]**: just a new *chiddush* (a new insight), but in this same *bina*.

blocks.title: Not from the Himalayas
blocks.text: Like innovation in computers. You notice it's not made by somebody who went to the Himalayas and meditated. It's made *davka* by the people who work with computers over and over again, and think about it, and think. And what do they think about? Obviously they couldn't have thought about the innovation; they didn't know the innovation. So they must have thought about what they already know. And yet they came up with an innovation.

blocks.title: From the Model T to the Pentium 4
blocks.text: The same with cars: the cars are getting better and better all the time, and a car right now is not like a Model T from the 1930s. Who came up with the better cars? The engineers who work for the car companies. Say a guy is now going to innovate a new thing in cars. How did he learn about cars? He went to college. What did he learn in college? The cars we already have. An engineer, in waterworks or electricity or whatever, or a doctor, learns *davka* what we already know, not what he's going to invent. And yet he invents a new thing, but the invention is *davka* in his field. An engineer in computers is not going to invent a new drug that will cure certain diseases; he's going to invent a better computer. They had the Pentium, now the Pentium II, then the Pentium III and the Pentium 4, and they're already thinking of a computer you won't even need a keyboard for, you'll just talk to it. How are they getting better and better? That is *chachma sheb'bina*.

When you go over the *bina sheb'bina*, this and this again: that is what he is talking about here, the activating power. It is the activating power of all the other powers; and in various places later he is going to explain that the activation of the lower powers, the *middos* (emotional attributes), also comes *davka* from *bina sheb'bina*. And the way it works, it has to be like this: *bina sheb'bina* within the *kli* of *daas*.

blocks.title: The would-be millionaire
blocks.text: Somebody is going to be a computer genius, but he's not really interested in computers in the first place. So why do you want to be a computer genius? "Well, I want to make computer inventions, and then I'll be a millionaire." He's probably not going to invent nothing new, because what he really wants is to be a millionaire; he's not interested in computers. He's going to college and stuff like that, and he's learning the information, but not the subject. He's doing the *bina sheb'bina*, but he doesn't have the *kli* of *daas*.

blocks.title: A glass with no water, water with no glass
blocks.text: The *daas* is also something. It's not totally nothing, but it's a *kli*, and a necessary *kli*. It's basically like a glass of water. If you don't have the glass, the water will just spill out. But on the other hand, if there's a guy in the desert dying of thirst and you give him a glass, that's not going to help him nothing. And if you just give him water without a glass, it'll spill in the sand, and you also won't help him nothing. Like if you just throw some water at him: "Hey, oh, you're thirsty? Here's some water." If you don't have the *kli* to hold the water in, it's useless; and the *kli* by itself is also useless.

**and this comes only through the *iyun* mentioned above**. This *chachma sheb'bina* does not come by itself, so that you can say, "Okay, I'm going to innovate something now." There's a tract from the Rebbe Rashab on how to learn Gemara, and basically what he says there is: you cannot go for *chiddushim*. You should not try to make a *chiddush*. If you're trying to make a *chiddush*, your *chiddush* will be what he calls a real *chiddush*. You know what a real *chiddush* is? It's invented. It was not told to Moshe Rabbeinu on Mount Sinai; you invented it out of your head. But the actual *chiddush* of a seasoned student comes *davka* when you don't go for the *chiddushim*: first you learn the text of the Gemara, then you learn it with Rashi. "What? That's what I'm going to learn, just the Talmud with Rashi? How am I going to be an innovator?" If you want to be an innovator, you'll never be an innovator. Just the opposite: it is *davka* when you do the *iyun* that the *chiddush* comes automatically.

So it is *davka* through the *iyun*, the *bina sheb'bina*, and that is what the whole chapter is about: the *bina sheb'bina* within the *kli* of *daas* is the activator of all the powers, whether above it or below it. In *Kuntres HaHispaalus* he explains that the *hispaalus* of the *middos* comes *davka* from *hisbonenus*. Here he explains that the higher powers come from it too. The real thing that you really want is the depth of *chachma*, the flash of light, or even higher, the unification with the ultimate unity, with the infinite light, and stuff like that. And what would you do? "Oh, I'll meditate on the light." But he says: no, it doesn't work like that.

It is *davka* the *iyun* that activates the powers below it; and as a matter of fact, even the *daas* is activated *davka* by the *bina sheb'bina*. You notice with us, for instance: we have a bigger *daas* in this (not a knowledge *daas*, a connection to it) than somebody who didn't learn as much as us. Why? Because we activated it up to the *Keser*, so the *daas* also gets activated, and that is *davka* because of the *bina sheb'bina*. The more you understand about something, and this is anything, the more your *daas* towards that thing is activated.

The only thing you have to remember: there are two kinds of *daas*. There's a negative *daas* too. When you understand more and more about something, you might understand that this is a bad thing, and then you'll have a *daas* that you want to stay away from it: the opposite of concentration. You don't want to think about it at all. Either way, the more you understand, the more the *daas* gets activated.

blocks.title: Red, green and blue: sorting a thing into its parts
blocks.text: **which sorts out all its parts clearly**: *iyun* means analysis, separating out all the parts of a thing according to its classifications. "Okay, this one is the red one, you put it here, and this one is the green one, you put it here. Now we have three red ones and two green ones, and here's a blue one." If you want to know how a television screen works, how the picture comes up: over here there's a red one, then two green ones, then a blue one. The same with everything. How does a personality work? You say: a personality is made up of intellect and emotions. That's your first separation, into two. What is intellect? There are three parts, *chachma*, *bina* and *daas*, and then there's the super-intellect of *Keser*. In the emotions there are seven; the basic division is love and fear. You separate it, and then you separate it more and more: within love there are also ten. **and is called *bina sheb'bina***: this analysis of the thing into its parts is called *bina sheb'bina*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך יוכל להוליד ולהתחכם להמציא הבנה והשגה חדשה,
phrases.en: Afterwards he can give birth, be wise, and come up with a new understanding and comprehension,

phrases.he: אבל רק בהשגה זו עצמה
phrases.en: but only in this comprehension itself,

phrases.he: שנקרא חכמה שבבינה,
phrases.en: which is called *chachma sheb'bina*.

phrases.he: אבל כתר דבינה הוא עומק המושג הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: But the *Keser* of *bina* is the depth of the concept mentioned above,

phrases.he: המגיע שרשו בעומק החכמה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: whose root reaches into the depth of *chachma*, as mentioned above.

blocks.text: **Afterwards**, only when he does this analysis, **he can give birth, be wise, and come up with a new understanding and comprehension**. It's *davka* the people who know the analysis of all the parts of a car who can come up with a better car. "I could not come up with a better car, because I have no idea how the motor works. I don't know what's going on in the motor." But somebody who knows every single part of the motor, *davka* somebody like that can come up with a better motor.

**but only in this comprehension itself**: only in a car. He can't innovate outside of his field. "Well, what about the Wright brothers?" It's still a machine, a traveling machine: they took a motor like a car's and put it on the airplane. That is really in a way a matter of *tevuna*, going from one field to another field, and it's also an innovation, but of *bina sheb'chachma* and stuff like that. The basic thing of *chachma sheb'bina* is just to make an innovation in this *hasaga* itself.

**But the *Keser* of *bina* is the depth of the concept mentioned above**. That is the *Keser* of *bina* itself, and in the *Keser* there is also an outer side of the *Keser* of *bina*, which is just to understand the explanation. But the root of the *Keser* of *bina* is in the depth of *chachma*: the real thing he wants to understand is not just the explanation, but the actual thing. That is what *chachma sheb'bina* is.

phrases.he: והבן בחכמה
phrases.en: And "understand with wisdom",

phrases.he: היינו ס''ג דע''ב, שהוא כח ההסבר בחכמה עצמה,
phrases.en: that is, *SaG* of *Ayin Beis*, is the power of explanation within *chachma* itself,

phrases.he: שיוכל להביאו בפנים מסבירות הרבה,
phrases.en: so that he can bring it out in many different explanations,

phrases.he: והוא למעלה מן ההשגה דבינה עדיין
phrases.en: and it is still above the comprehension of *bina*.

blocks.text: **that is, *SaG* of *Ayin Beis*, is the power of explanation within *chachma* itself**: *bina* of *chachma*, the *hiyuli* (raw potential), the inherent power of explanation within a *chachma*. When you understand something beyond just the explanation, and you have it in the way of the *ayin* of *chachma*, it is inherent in this *chachma* that you could explain it. You didn't explain it at all yet, but if somebody asks you, you'll be able to explain it, and not in just one way: **in many different explanations**. When he goes past the *omek hamusag* of *bina* into the actual *chachma* of the thing, it is inherent in the *bina* of *chachma* that he can then explain it in various ways. **and it is still above the comprehension of *bina***: it's not that he actually explained it. It is a *hiyuli* for explanation.

phrases.he: ומה שאמרו נבונים לא אשתכחו,
phrases.en: But what they said, "Men of understanding were not to be found,"

phrases.he: שהוא המבין דבר מתוך דבר דוקא
phrases.en: means one who understands one thing from another, *davka*;

phrases.he: היינו מצד שרש כח זה דהבן בחכמה שמגיע בעומק דחכמה הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: that is, from the root of this power of "understand with wisdom", which reaches into the depth of *chachma*, as said above:

phrases.he: על כן יוכל להבין דבר חכמה אחרת לגמרי מתוך דבר חכמה זאת
phrases.en: therefore he can understand an altogether different wisdom from this wisdom,

blocks.text: **But what they said, "Men of understanding were not to be found,"** is something besides the power of explanation, because *bina sheb'chachma* has two things in it. The power of explanation is *bina sheb'chachma* going downwards: he can bring this *chachma* into various explanations of *bina*. But the "and" here means "but": what they said, men of understanding were not to be found, they didn't mean that there are no people who could explain it. He's saying that's something... (the side of the tape ends here).

**therefore he can understand an altogether different wisdom from this wisdom**: the inner power of *bina* of *chachma* reaches into the depth of *chachma*, into the aquifer, as we said, and that's why he can understand a different *chachma* from this *chachma*.

He's telling you not one thing here but really three things about the power of *bina* of *chachma*. One, going downwards: the inherent power of explanation, to bring a *chachma* out into an explanation, is *davka* from the power of *bina* of *chachma*. Two, the real, inner thing of *bina* of *chachma*: to understand one thing from another, a deeper wisdom from an external wisdom. And three: since he goes into the aquifer, he'll be able to understand a different wisdom from this wisdom, a different field altogether. From this field he'll be able to carry it into a different field. Why? Because he understood it all the way into the aquifer, and that's the source of all the wisdoms. So it can go down, it can go up, and it can go sideways, like a width.

blocks.title: The Wright brothers' bicycle chain
blocks.text: It's a width: he can bring it into a different wisdom altogether, though that other wisdom can be on the same level as this one. Like what we said about the Wright brothers. They were bicycle makers, they were interested in cars, and they brought it into airplanes. They were not really total *navonim* (men of understanding), but it's good for a *mashal*, an external *mashal*. What they did is they looked into it. They didn't just look at a motor as a car motor; they looked into its root, a supplier of power: the same as it could supply power to a car, it could supply power to an airplane. And being bicycle makers, they knew how to make those chains and the gears with teeth in them that connect into the chain; the airplanes aren't made like that now, but the original airplanes had those things connecting to the propeller. So they took from bicycles to airplanes.

Why? Because they didn't look at a chain the way somebody on a more external level would, who knows how to make a bicycle and would never think how it applies to something else. They thought into the root of it. They didn't see it as just a bicycle: they saw it as a way to move the energy from the feet to the wheel, through the chain and the gear. They saw the inner point of the thing, a way to move energy from one thing to another thing.

phrases.he: שזהו למעלה במדריגה מן החכם,
phrases.en: which is higher in level than the wise man,

phrases.he: דהיינו מגופה של המצאות החכמה זו מאין,
phrases.en: that is, than the very discovery of this wisdom from *ayin*,

phrases.he: שאינו מבין ממנה חכמה ושכל אחר
phrases.en: from which he does not understand another wisdom and idea.

blocks.text: **which is higher in level than the wise man**. The outer level of *bina sheb'chachma*, explaining it outwards, is lower than the actual *chachma sheb'chachma*. But the inner level of *bina sheb'chachma*, the *navon*, is higher than the wise man. Why is that? Because a *navon* is *bina sheb'chachma*, and a wise man is really *chachma sheb'chachma*. **that is, than the very discovery of this wisdom from *ayin***: he just has an invention. The *navon* might not be able to come up with a new invention, but he can take an old invention and come up with a whole new thing. In a way it has a higher source; and not only that, it can reach into a depth higher than the *chachma* itself, into understanding one thing from another.

Remember, we're talking about what *hisbonenus* is in terms of *Chassidus*. This understanding of one thing from another is what he talks about later, when he says "we will rejoice and be glad in You, *mamash*": it is with this power of *bina sheb'chachma*. The *bina sheb'bina* will activate the *chachma sheb'bina*, and the *chachma sheb'bina* will activate the *bina sheb'chachma*. And then when you have the *chachma* itself, the seeing, as with an eye, he'll be able to understand not just the *seder hishtalshelus* but one thing from another, higher than the *seder hishtalshelus*: from the *seder hishtalshelus* he'll understand what is deeper than the *seder hishtalshelus*. That's basically what he's talking about here.

phrases.he: (ומכל מקום מה שבהשגה דבינה מבין השגה חדשה מתוך ההשגה זו,
phrases.en: (Even so, that in the comprehension of *bina* one understands a new comprehension from this comprehension

phrases.he: שרשה בהבן דחכמה,
phrases.en: has its root in "understanding" of *chachma*,

phrases.he: שמבין דבר מתוך דבר, רק שזה בהעלם מקור השכל
phrases.en: which understands one thing from another, only here it is in the hiddenness of the source of the intellect;

phrases.he: כו' ודי למבין).
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.)

blocks.text: **has its root in "understanding" of *chachma***: what he is saying is that the root of *chachma sheb'bina* is in *bina sheb'chachma*. **only here it is in the hiddenness of the source of the intellect**: one of them is in the hidden part of the intellect, and the other is in the revealed part of the intellect.

sections.title: The order of the levels, and the student's way: up the length to the depth
sections.summary: *Hisbonenus* starts with *bina sheb'bina*, which gives a concept its length; *chachma sheb'bina* gives it width; and how long and wide it gets depends on its depth, the *Keser* of *bina*. The main point, which the text leaves unsaid, runs the other way: the student reaches the depth only by going up one length at a time, the way Moshiach will split the river.

phrases.he: ונמצא סדר המדרגות כך הם,
phrases.en: So the order of the levels is as follows:

phrases.he: בחינת עיון הנזכר לעיל לעמוד על בוריו כו'
phrases.en: The *iyun* mentioned above, to stand on it clearly [in all its parts],

phrases.he: נקרא בינה שבבינה,
phrases.en: is called *bina sheb'bina*:

phrases.he: להבחין תכלית ההבחנה בפנימיות וחיצוניות
phrases.en: to examine to the utmost of examination, the inner and the outer.

blocks.text: **So the order of the levels is as follows:** now he's going to tell you what *hisbonenus* is, how you do *hisbonenus*. First of all, you start off with *bina sheb'bina*: to go through the analysis of all the separate parts. That is called *bina sheb'bina*, **to examine to the utmost of examination, the inner and the outer** of whatever it is that you're examining.

phrases.he: וגם מזה יוכל להיות בחינת האורך,
phrases.en: And from this can also come the length:

phrases.he: להוריד ההשגה בלבושים רבים עד שתתגשם להשגות התינוק כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: to bring the comprehension down into many garments until it takes shape for the grasp of a child, as said above;

phrases.he: אבל לא בחינת הרוחב בהסברים שונים לכל צד כו'
phrases.en: but not the width, in different explanations to every side.

blocks.text: **And from this can also come the length** of *bina*: to explain it down into *meshalim*, until a child can grasp it. So *bina sheb'bina* is also the length of *bina*. **but not the width, in different explanations to every side**: different explanations are already an innovation. That's not *bina sheb'bina*; it's *davka* the length. *Bina sheb'bina* means you understand within this explanation, only along this length.

phrases.he: ואחר כך מבחינת חכמה שבבינה,
phrases.en: Then, from *chachma sheb'bina*:

phrases.he: להמציא חדשות בהשגה א' כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: coming up with new things, but in one comprehension, as said above,

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא רוחב,
phrases.en: that is what is called width;

phrases.he: וממנו כח דבינה שבבינה העושה בחינת אורך
phrases.en: and from it, the power of *bina sheb'bina* that makes the length.

blocks.text: The width is *chachma sheb'bina*. **coming up with new things, but in one comprehension**: *davka* in this *hasaga*. **that is what is called width**: you're giving a new twist to the thing, you understand a new matter. **and from it, the power of *bina sheb'bina* that makes the length**: the way you come up with a new explanation is *davka* when you have the *chachma sheb'bina*. When you understand a new twist on a thing, you can make a whole new length when you go and analyze that twist.

phrases.he: אבל שיעור האורך והרוחב דחכמה ובינה שבבינה,
phrases.en: But the measure of the length and the width, of *chachma* and *bina sheb'bina*,

phrases.he: הוא תלוי בבחינת עומק המושג שנקרא כתר דבינה,
phrases.en: depends on the depth of the concept, which is called the *Keser* of *bina*;

phrases.he: וכנראה בחוש שלפי ערך העומק כך יהיה ערך הרוחב והאורך בכל השגת דבר מה
phrases.en: and we see plainly that as the depth is, so will the width and the length be, in grasping anything at all;

phrases.he: וד"ל).
phrases.en: and this is enough for one who understands.)

blocks.title: Chess and checkers
blocks.text: **depends on the depth of the concept, which is called the *Keser* of *bina***. In *Chassidus*, in what we're learning here, the length and the width can be fantastic. Why? Because the depth is fantastic. Something like understanding how to play chess: there's a big width and length, not like this, but more than checkers. Everybody understands chess is a deeper game than checkers, so there are all kinds of books written with strategies on chess. In checkers you can also write, but how much can you write already? Not like chess. Why? Because the depth of chess is bigger, so the length and the width will be bigger.

blocks.title: The doctor who went through the length
blocks.text: And not only that: it works vice versa too. You don't get to the depth without going through the length and the width. You don't get to the depth by concentrating on it; it's *davka* when you go through the length and the width. A doctor who learned for seven years obviously knows more about medicine than Rabbi Markel does: he knows all the explanations, where all the bones are, where all the organs are. "Sometimes I consult her about things in *Chassidus*, where it talks about the liver and stuff like that," or how the brain is made, because she knows the actual physical makeup of these things, and she explains to him how the liver works. Why? Because she's a doctor. She went through the length.

sensitivity.reason: Mentions a woman doctor he consults about Chassidus, apparently someone close to him.
sensitivity.publishable: And not only that: it works vice versa too. You don't get to the depth without going through the length and the width. You don't get to the depth by concentrating on it; it's *davka* when you go through the length and the width. A doctor who learned for seven years obviously knows more about medicine than a layman: he knows all the explanations, where all the bones are, where all the organs are. When *Chassidus* talks about the liver, or how the brain is made, a doctor can explain the actual physical makeup of these things. Why? Because a doctor went through the length.
sensitivity.publishableTitle: The doctor who went through the length

blocks.text: Now a doctor who knows not only occidental medicine, but also oriental medicine and homeopathic medicine and other kinds of medicine, has a width. He might be a better doctor than somebody who only wants to know one way of looking at medicine, who knows only one explanation. Because he has a bigger width, he might have a bigger depth also. So it works both ways.

sensitivity.reason: Suggests a doctor who also knows oriental and homeopathic medicine may be the better doctor.
sensitivity.publishable: Someone who knows a field in more than one way has a width, and because he has a bigger width he might have a bigger depth also. So it works both ways.

blocks.text: According to the *omek hamusag* of a thing, that's how much length and width you're going to have; and vice versa, how far you can get into the depth is *davka* according to how much you went through the length and the width. **and we see plainly that as the depth is, so will the width and the length be, in grasping anything at all**: in any kind of thing, *davka* according to how deep the subject matter is, that's how much length and width there will be in it. And really, basically, it's also the other way around.

Which he doesn't say here, but it is really the main point, the real main point of this chapter: not so much that the length and width are according to the depth, but that reaching into the depth is according to how much you went through the length and the width. *Davka* through the *bina sheb'bina*, and really *davka* through the length, because you shouldn't make *chiddushim*. He said it here in a way from up to down: from the depth comes the width, and from the width comes the length. That's a teacher teaching it. But we are really going from down up, and in terms of the student, the student should concentrate *davka* on the length.

If he tries to concentrate on a width, he'll get nothing; he'll just jump around. Like these guys: one day they learn physics, they want to be a physicist. The next day, "Yeah, you know what? I want to be a chemist." The next day, "Oh, you know what? I decided I want to be in computers." The next day, "No, I want to make airplanes." Like what he says later about someone who has a wide *daas* but doesn't have a deep *daas*; really, someone like that doesn't have a *daas* at all. It's a wide *daas*, all spread. There's people who know about baseball, they know about football, they know a little bit about this, but there's nothing they're really into. Ultimately they don't really know anything too much about anything, because they don't have a deep *daas* into one particular thing that really turns them on.

That's the basic thing: *daas* has to hold you onto the length. A width is multiple lengths, and in order to learn, you have to do *davka* *bina sheb'bina*, which means a single length. The same with people who have learned various Kabbalistic stuff: here it tells them one thing, and they say, "What do you mean, *chachma* is this? It says *chachma* is not this." But that's a different length. In order to learn this length, you have to forget about that length; and if you try to put the two of them together, you're not ready for the width yet, till you go through the length. When you go through the length of *Shaar HaYichud*, then you'll be able to understand how *chachma* does have letters and doesn't have letters, how *chachma* is a point and yet has dimensions: it's talking about two different aspects, two different lengths, and when you put the two together, it gives you a width. So the order of the levels goes *davka* from *bina sheb'bina*: you have to sit and learn a length and forget about the other length.

And then from that comes *chachma sheb'bina*: now you'll start seeing new things, but *davka* in this explanation. From that it will come into the power of *bina sheb'chachma*, which is really the outer side of *chachma*, not the inner *bina sheb'chachma*: you'll start reaching the *hiyuli* of many different explanations. And from that it will activate the power of *chachma sheb'chachma*, and that will activate the power of *bina sheb'chachma* going up into *taalumos chachma*, to understand one thing from another.

By the way, that whole thing about a river: it's not talking about a river. That is the matter of *bina sheb'chachma*, to understand from the *mashal* to the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for). And when we say a length, it's not the same as the length of a river; not a physical length. The length, from up to down, when you go from down to up, is to understand a thing from inside of a thing, along the length.

blocks.title: Moshiach will split the river lengthwise
blocks.text: That's what it says, that when Moshiach comes he will open up the river. Moshe Rabbeinu opened up the sea; Moshiach will open up the river, lengthwise, not sideways. As a matter of fact it says so explicitly: he'll open up the river and it'll become seven streams. He'll split it along the length, not along the width. When Moshiach comes he'll open up the river, and then you'll go up the length into the depth. If you take a boat up the river, you end up at the source, by the spring; and if you keep going, you'll end up in the aquifer. He'll open it up all the way to the aquifer, so that the aquifer will be revealed, and that's what it says, that the wellsprings of the deep will come out. That's the Flood: the hidden aquifer bursting out into the revealed, with the lower depths and with the upper depths, which are also hidden. The windows of heaven will be opened: right now it's a window, and he'll open it up so it's totally open. Like a ceiling with a little hole in it, and then the whole ceiling breaks down and all the water on top of it floods everything. That's what we're going to expect very soon.

blocks.question: Why does he mention *Ayin Beis* of *SaG* and *SaG* of *Ayin Beis* here, when the explanation would be exactly the same without them?
blocks.text: Right now, the best thing is to skip that whole thing. If you don't skip it, you'll just be stuck with it and you won't understand nothing. Later on, when we get to chapter 10 and so on, he speaks of the yud of the *SaG* (in chapter 12, maybe; he doesn't remember which chapter), and then we'll start understanding what it's talking about. Partly it's because in his days it was written for people who were kabbalists. And later, the whole matter of the Names, how this Name goes into its various forms, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG* and the rest: right now we have a very vague understanding of what each letter means, just the general idea of what a Name is, and later on we're going to understand why he said it. There's a reason; it's not for nothing. It's there for later. Right now, the way we're understanding it, it's enough to understand *chachma* of *bina* and *bina* of *chachma*.

And by the way, this is why we want so much to turn everybody else onto this. We're on a 007 thing (actually, since we're in the sixth millennium, a 006 thing): a need-to-know basis. It was like this by the prophets too: it says that when the *Aibershter* (G-d) was angry at the Jews, Moshe Rabbeinu didn't get prophecy. When we get these other people to learn and they start asking this question, we're going to have to know the answer, and at that point we'll know the answer. At that point we'll be able to sit in our retreat in the Catskills, or on the Golan Heights or wherever, with a whole yeshiva and all the books, and look it up in *Etz Chaim*: what it says about the *Ayin Beis* of the *SaG* and the *SaG* of the *Ayin Beis*, what the yud of the *Ayin Beis* means, and why in *Ayin Beis* the vav is spelled vav-yud-vav and in *SaG* vav-alef-vav. Then we'll understand.

But right now basically the answer is that this book was written for kabbalists. That's why Rabbi Markel mostly tells people not to learn the Reb Hillel Paritcher: Reb Hillel Paritcher is really more complicated than this, and brings in a lot more Kabbalistic things. In a way, part of what he is doing is this. People had the same complaint against the Mitteler Rebbe as they had against the *Rambam*: he didn't seem to bring sources. "Where is he getting all this from? Where is he coming up with this crazy stuff? That's not what it says in *Etz Chaim*." In *Etz Chaim* it says *Ayin Beis* of *SaG*, *SaG* of *Ayin Beis*, and he is talking about something you can apply to building cars and bicycles. What does stuff from *Etz Chaim* have to do with building cars or bicycles? "Hey, told you: that's the *Ayin Beis* of the *SaG* and the *SaG* of the *Ayin Beis*." So in Reb Hillel Paritcher a lot of it is apologetics; not exactly apologetics, showing how this really comes from Kabbala. But to do that, you have to know the Kabbala.

So in Reb Hillel Paritcher a lot of it is apologetics; not exactly apologetics, showing how this really comes from Kabbala. But to do that, you have to know the Kabbala.

blocks.text: At the level we're holding right now, that's the best explanation: this book is like a Torah scroll. The story of Yosef and his brothers is a story for little kids, so therefore you should treat your brother nicely; it's on the level of a big rabbi in halacha; and it's on the level of the biggest kabbalist, the *Arizal*. The story of Yosef is on all those levels. This book too: it's on a level that a brand new guy who doesn't know from nothing can sit with it and learn it.

blocks.title: What the Rebbe Rashab was proudest of
blocks.text: And the biggest: what was the Rebbe Rashab so proud of the Frierdiker Rebbe for? You'd think there should be many things he would be proud of him for. The thing he was the most proud of was that he read the *Shaar HaYichud* without his father telling him to, and wrote a commentary on it. And Rabbi Markel doesn't think the way the Frierdiker Rebbe and the Rebbe Rashab read this book was the same way we are reading it. So this book is written on every level.

As a matter of fact, when the *Aibershter* decided that He's going to be the *Aibershter*, and He wanted to know how to be the *Aibershter*, He had to read this book to find out who He is. Another story, with Jackie Mason. Jackie Mason goes: "I went to a psychologist. I told him, so what am I doing here? He says, well, I'm going to help you find yourself. What do you mean find myself? I'm right over here! I know where I am! He says, no, I'm going to help you find out who you are. What do you mean? You mean I'm not me? I thought I was me. So maybe really you're me and I'm you, so you give me the 50 bucks!"

sensitivity.reason: Jokes that G-d had to read this book to find out who He is; it sets up the identity-crisis joke of the next block.
sensitivity.publishable: Another story, with Jackie Mason. Jackie Mason goes: "I went to a psychologist. I told him, so what am I doing here? He says, well, I'm going to help you find yourself. What do you mean find myself? I'm right over here! I know where I am! He says, no, I'm going to help you find out who you are. What do you mean? You mean I'm not me? I thought I was me. So maybe really you're me and I'm you, so you give me the 50 bucks!"

blocks.text: So when the *Aibershter* had an identity crisis and wanted to find out who He is, all He had to do was read the *Shaar HaYichud*. This is written even for the *Aibershter*, *mamash*. "I know it sounds kind of funny, what do you mean written for the *Aibershter*," but really it's written even for the *Aibershter*. And that's why the *Aibershter* wanted the world: because He wanted to get the explanation *davka* from idiots, the way we understand it. And when we sit here, like today: you had a three-way conference call, and it was actually a four-way conference call. One of the lines was arranged for the *Aibershter*, and He was listening in on it too, and He found out a whole bunch of things. He says, "Oh, so that's who I am. Maybe you'll give me the 50 bucks."

sensitivity.reason: Jokes that G-d had an identity crisis and owes the psychologist's fee.
