That's why the *Aibershter* wanted the world: He wanted to get the explanation *davka* from us, the way we understand it. And when we sit here, like today, on what you had as a three-way conference call, it was actually a four-way conference call: one of the lines was arranged for the *Aibershter*, and He was listening in on it too.

sections.title: Daas is the dive, not the depth: the bond that holds a concept
sections.summary: Concentration is not the depth of a concept but what carries one to it, as a dive carries a diver to the ocean floor; and it works only after the *iyun* has given it the explanation. *Daas* has length (attention span, holding a long idea), width and depth, and its depth, as with the boy who loved hockey, draws out its length.

phrases.he: ולפ"ז מה שקוראים העולם העמקת הדעת,
phrases.en: Accordingly, what the world calls *ha'amakas hadaas* (concentration)

phrases.he: אין זה גופה של העמקה,
phrases.en: is not the body of the depth itself,

phrases.he: כמו עומק המושג דבינה,
phrases.en: such as the depth of the concept in *bina*,

phrases.he: שלזה לא יש שייכות לדעת
phrases.en: which has nothing to do with *daas*.

blocks.title: The dive and the floor of the ocean
blocks.text: So that was about *chachma* and *bina* and all this stuff; now he is going to be talking about *daas*. **Accordingly, what the world calls *ha'amakas hadaas* (concentration)**, according to what we said before, **is not the body of the depth itself**. It's not the actual essence of the depth. It is the deepening, but not the actual depth. Like when you take a deep dive off a board: the concentration is like the dive, and the actual depth is the depth of the pool, where you're going to. Or those people you see when you go to Hawaii: they throw money off the boat, and those guys jump off their little boats and go down to get it. The depth is the floor of the ocean; the concentration is the dive that gets them there. So concentration is not the actual depth; it's the thing that gets you to the depth.

**such as the depth of the concept in *bina***, the actual depth of the actual concept, **which has nothing to do with *daas***. This has nothing to do with concentration. To understand the depth of how computers work, when you go to school and learn, you have to concentrate in order to get it. But really that has nothing to do with concentration: the actual concept, the *omek hamusag*, has nothing to do with concentration.

phrases.he: אך הדעת הוא בחינת התקשרות הרגשתו במושג ביותר,
phrases.en: Rather, *daas* is the connecting of one's feeling into the concept very much;

phrases.he: והוא שמביא לידי בחינת העמקה במושג,
phrases.en: and it brings one into delving into the concept,

phrases.he: אחר בחינת העיון הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: after the *iyun* mentioned above,

phrases.he: שהוא רק כמו בחינת כלי לעומק ההשגה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: for it is only like a *kli* for the depth of the comprehension, as said above.

phrases.he: וגם בדעת יש אורך ורוחב ועומק,
phrases.en: *Daas* too has length, width and depth:

phrases.he: כמו יש מי שדעתו קצרה
phrases.en: there is one whose *daas* is short,

phrases.he: ויש שדעתו ארוכה
phrases.en: one whose *daas* is long,

phrases.he: ויש שדעתו רחבה ולא ארוכה
phrases.en: one whose *daas* is wide but not long,

phrases.he: ודעת חזק
phrases.en: a strong *daas*

phrases.he: או דעת קל
phrases.en: or a light *daas*,

phrases.he: כנשים שדעתן קלות,
phrases.en: like women, whose *daas* is light:

phrases.he: הוא בלתי עומק הדעת וממילא דעתו קצרה כו'
phrases.en: that is without depth of *daas*, and so his *daas* is short.

blocks.text: **Rather, *daas* is the connecting of one's feeling into the concept very much**: concentration, in other words, to connect your feeling into the concept very much. **and it brings one into delving into the concept**, **after the *iyun* mentioned above**: once you know all the details, that's still not enough. If the *bina* is a *bina* without *daas*, if you don't concentrate on it: there are two kids sitting in a classroom, and one is getting A's and one is getting D's. They both heard exactly the same explanation; the teacher gave the same explanation to both of them. But since in one there was *daas* and in the other there was no *daas*, one of them got to the *omek hamusag* and one of them didn't.

But nonetheless, it's only after the *iyun*. If one kid says, "Well, since I concentrate so hard, I'll just stay home and concentrate," that's not going to work, because he didn't get the explanation. **for it is only like a *kli* for the depth of the comprehension**: the *daas* is only a *kli* to get deeply into the *hasaga*, but you have to have the *hasaga*.

***Daas* too has length, width and depth**: **there is one whose *daas* is short**, meaning the attention span. One of the things in learning *Chassidus* is the attention span, a long *daas* and a short *daas*. In *Ayin Beis*, for instance: both of these books are a *hemshech* (a continuous series of discourses). What does a *hemshech* mean? That in order to do the proper *hisbonenus* of the *daas*, after you have the *omek hamusag* in your brain, you have to be able to hold the entire book in your head at one shot. Or, if not the entire book, at least a certain amount of it: chapter one, or this little paragraph about *daas* that we're learning now. In order to think about it, you have to be able to hold this whole thing in your head at one shot. That's one side of the length of *daas*.

And the other side of it is: how long can you concentrate? "If you have an attention span of three seconds, I won't be able to learn with you." It's not going to help; after three seconds you're going to be somewhere else. For our classes, for instance, you have to have an attention span of somewhere between half an hour and an hour. You have to have a *daas* to leave everything, put your whole *daas* into just the class, and take everything else away for about half an hour to an hour.

They did research: the maximum attention span of an American is about ten to fifteen minutes. They did it for the TVs; that's why they put the commercials. After about ten minutes, even if it's a very interesting program, people tend to lose their attention. In movies too: if you keep a certain scene going too long, you have to switch to another scene, otherwise you're going to lose your audience. Like those Indian movies: very long, long, drawn out; an American won't be able to sit through it. Or some of these artsy Scandinavian movies.

sensitivity.reason: Generalises about Americans' attention span and pokes fun at Indian and Scandinavian films.
sensitivity.publishable: Research says the attention span of a television audience is about ten to fifteen minutes; that's why they put the commercials there. In movies too: if you keep a certain scene going too long, you have to switch to another scene, otherwise you're going to lose your audience.

blocks.text: So a short *daas* means, first of all, a short attention span, and also the power of holding on to an idea in your mind, how long you can hold on to it. When you go through *Ayin Beis*, a particular idea can be 50, 60, 70, 80, 100 chapters. You're going through it, you're learning something, and after a while you don't even know what he's talking about anymore, because you're already holding ten chapters in your mind and your mind is already blowing up. You have to have an incredible length of *daas*, to keep your concentration on a fantastically long idea. Some of the ideas there are 30 to 100 chapters long, but really it's even longer: the whole thing is one idea. Rabbi Markel says he knows he has a longer *daas* than most people, "because I have the *daas* from here"; and still, sometimes he can't even hold on to part of an idea there, 30 chapters long. "I go through the thing and after a while I have no idea what he's talking about. I forget what he was talking about before. I can't hold a whole thing in my mind, because my *daas* is not that long."

**one whose *daas* is long**: there are some people who have a much longer attention span; they can sit with one thing for a much longer time. And in general, you notice, kids have a very short attention span. **one whose *daas* is wide but not long**: like we were saying before, he knows a little bit of everything, but he can't stay with one thing for a long time. **a strong *daas***: he's very opinionated. **or a light *daas***: it's very easy to change his opinion.

**like women, whose *daas* is light**. It doesn't mean there aren't some women who have a stronger *daas* than certain men. But in general, what you'll find is this. Take a frum woman like your wife (he says to the student): if she says, "What do you mean I have a light *daas*?", you can show her that most men don't have as heavy a *daas* as she does. But we're talking about people on the same level. That's because she's a frum lady who's into learning, so she doesn't have such a light *daas* as some guy who's into rock and roll. But if you look at that guy's girlfriend, you'll see her *daas* is even lighter than his. Or if you see some Rebbetzin, the wife of one of the great rabbis, you say, "What do you mean? Look at her, she has a bigger *daas* than you do." He says, "Yeah, but look at her in comparison to her husband, and it might not be like that. It's according to the level."

sensitivity.reason: Explains "women, whose daas is light" with comparisons between women and men (the rock-and-roll guy's girlfriend, a Rebbetzin and her husband), and brings in the student's wife.
sensitivity.publishable: **like women, whose *daas* is light**. It doesn't mean there aren't some women who have a stronger *daas* than certain men; we're talking about people on the same level. It's according to the level.

blocks.text: So what does a light *daas* mean? **that is without depth of *daas*, and so his *daas* is short**. Since he isn't very deeply into the thing, his *daas* is also short, like a little kid's. It's the same thing as we said about *bina*: the depth brings about the width and the length.

blocks.title: The boy who loved hockey
blocks.text: You notice that if somebody is really deep into a certain thing, it changes. Rabbi Markel knew a kid who looked like he had no *daas* at all. He had no attention span for nothing; in school he had no attention span for nothing. But he loved hockey. He had these books on hockey with whole pages of statistics; it looked like a whole mathematical book. And in mathematics he was doing lousy. But when it was hockey, the statistics of what this guy shot and how many points he scored, he could sit with it for hours. So you see: according to the depth of the *daas* you have in something, the length becomes longer. He'll have a much longer attention span.

phrases.he: והפרש זה בין קלי הדעת לעומקי הדעת, בין גדול לקטן ידוע,
phrases.en: The difference between those of light *daas* and those of deep *daas* is known, as between an adult and a child:

phrases.he: שהתינוק שדעתו קל,
phrases.en: a child's *daas* is light;

phrases.he: היינו שאין בו כח המרגיש והתקשרות כלל לדבר זה שמבין או רוצה בו, רק בחיצוניות מאד
phrases.en: that is, he has no feeling and no connection at all to the thing he understands or wants, only in a very external way;

phrases.he: על כן יתפתה להיפוכו,
phrases.en: therefore he is easily talked into the opposite.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן הגדול שדעתו עמוקה באותו דבר שמבין או רוצה בו,
phrases.en: An adult, by contrast, whose *daas* is deep in the thing he understands or wants:

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא העמקת הדעת,
phrases.en: that is what is called *ha'amakas hadaas*;

phrases.he: שממילא נמשך אורך הדעת ורוחב הדעת כנזכר לעיל בבינה.
phrases.en: and from it, automatically, come the length of *daas* and the width of *daas*, as said above about *bina*.

blocks.text: **The difference between those of light *daas* and those of deep *daas* is known, as between an adult and a child**: people who have a light *daas* and people who have a deep *daas* are like an older person and a younger person. **a child's *daas* is light**: he doesn't have such a strong, real feeling or connection to the thing, **only in a very external way**.

That's why a kid wants, he wants, he wants this toy, and you get him the toy, and two seconds later he's already forgotten about it. Why? He wanted it so much! Because the connection was only in a very external way; it was not really touching him on an inner level. **An adult, by contrast, whose *daas* is deep in the thing he understands or wants**, like a communist or something like that: he is connected to it in a much more inner way. That's called *omek hadaas*, the connection to the thing, **and from it, automatically, come the length of *daas* and the width of *daas***. Somebody who is really into the thing deeply will automatically have the long attention span, will be able to hold long ideas in his head, and will also have the width of seeing it in many different ways, as it said about *bina*: the length and the width come from the depth.

sections.title: Deep daas squeezes the whole mind into one point, and daas and bina depend on each other
sections.summary: The sign of deep *daas* is a face *farkvetsht* around one point, the opposite of *iyun*, which spreads into every detail; a class on *daas* thinks of nothing but *daas*. Point by point, that brings one to the root of the concept, up to *daas elyon*, which unites *chachma* and *bina*. *Daas* without *bina* is the *daas* of *Tohu*, and *bina* without *daas* is not learned.

phrases.he: וסימן להעמקת הדעת הוא אשר נראה כענין צמצום וכיווץ כלי המוח,
phrases.en: The sign of *ha'amakas hadaas* is that it looks like a contracting and squeezing of the vessel of the brain,

phrases.he: לעוצם עומק התקשרותו במושכל,
phrases.en: from how deeply he is connected to the concept

phrases.he: (בל"א ער איז דרינן פר נומען פר קוועצט שטארק
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: he is all taken up in it, *farkvetsht* strongly,

phrases.he: זייער ביז עס3 איז זייער מצומצם
phrases.en: very much, until he is very contracted,

phrases.he: רק בתנוע' אחת4 וסקירה אחת לבד כו')
phrases.en: only in one movement and one look);

phrases.he: שמזה דוקא בא עצם עומק השגה על ידי העיון דבינה
phrases.en: and from this *davka* comes the very depth of comprehension through the *iyun* of *bina*,

blocks.text: **The sign of *ha'amakas hadaas* is that it looks like a contracting and squeezing of the vessel of the brain**: the external sign that somebody is concentrating. It looks like he's kvetching up his brain, as far as how deeply he is connected to the concept.

blocks.title: Rabbi Raichik's nose through the tallis
blocks.text: Like Rabbi Raichik, may he rest in peace. You know Rabbi Raichik had a long, sharp nose. Rabbi Markel saw sometimes, when he davened, that he would concentrate so hard his nose would come out through the back of his tallis. That's this sign: you kvetch up your face. As he kvetches up his face, it almost looks like he's trying to kvetch up his brain. That's the external sign of it.

sensitivity.reason: A joke about the nose of a named, recently deceased rabbi.
sensitivity.publishable: Like Rabbi Raichik, may he rest in peace. Rabbi Markel saw sometimes, when he davened, how hard he would concentrate. That's this sign: you kvetch up your face. As he kvetches up his face, it almost looks like he's trying to kvetch up his brain. That's the external sign of it.

blocks.text: **in Yiddish: he is all taken up in it, *farkvetsht* strongly**, very much, **until he is very contracted**, **only in one movement and one look**: he is totally focused on one thing, and the external side of it is that it looks like he's *farkvetsht*-ing his brain. His whole face gets *farkvetsht*.

**and from this *davka* comes the very depth of comprehension**: *davka* from getting totally *farkvetsht* into the one matter. Right now, for instance: we said the whole book is really one *hemshech*, and finally, to really do the *iyun*, you have to hold the whole book in your head. But right now we're totally *farkvetsht* only into the matter of *daas*.

It's a funny thing: this book is always a *mashal* on itself. Whatever you're talking about, you can use it as a *mashal* of what you're talking about. So right now we're totally *farkvetsht* about *daas*. We're not thinking about the *Malchus* of *tevuna*, or how the letters come out, how Leah comes out, or what's the difference between *chachma* and *bina*, or how the crowns are. Not only that: if we would think about it, it would take away from our delving into this.

If we would now start discussing all kinds of other things... It says, "A good student asks according to the matter." If now all of a sudden you start asking, "Oh yeah, but what about the *Malchus* of *tevuna*?" "What are you talking about, *Malchus* of *tevuna*? We're talking about *daas*." "Yeah, yeah, okay, but what about the *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and what about the yud of the *SaG*, and what about this and what about that?" It would actually take away, and you would learn nothing. What brings about the delving into the concept (not the delving of the *daas*: the real *omek hamusag* we're trying to learn here) is that we're *farkvetsht*-ing ourselves *davka* into this matter and leaving aside all the other matters. **through the *iyun* of *bina***: the *iyun* of *bina* means to cut it up into little pieces. But now we are only going into the one piece.

phrases.he: שהוא היפך הצמצום והכיווץ,
phrases.en: which is the opposite of contraction and squeezing;

phrases.he: שהרי העיון דבינה, גם שעומד ומעוכב בצמצום וכיווץ בתחלתו,
phrases.en: for the *iyun* of *bina*, though at its start it stands and is held in contraction and squeezing,

phrases.he: אבל מיד מתפשת לרוחב הרבה בכל פרטי חלקיו,
phrases.en: at once spreads out wide into all the details of its parts,

phrases.he: בהבחנת פרטיות הרבה כידוע
phrases.en: examining many particulars, as is known.

blocks.text: **which is the opposite of contraction and squeezing**. What does it mean? **for the *iyun* of *bina*, though at its start it stands and is held in contraction and squeezing**, in the beginning talking about one point, **at once spreads out wide into all the details of its parts**: the *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and the letters, and outer and inner, and the angels. That's the whole thing of *hisbonenus*: to cut it up into all its sections and all its parts. And this is exactly the opposite: we're not going to go into everything; we're only going to go into *daas*, nothing else. If this was a class with students and he was the teacher, and somebody brought up a question about the *Malchus* of *tevuna* now: "Hey, what are you talking about? Why are you interrupting the class?" **examining many particulars, as is known**.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן הצמצום והכיווץ דהעמקת הדעת,
phrases.en: But the contraction and squeezing of *ha'amakas hadaas*

phrases.he: אדרבה, הוא רק הצמצום,
phrases.en: is, on the contrary, only contraction:

phrases.he: שהוא הקיבוץ והאסיפה מכל כח שכלו להתקשר רק במושכל זה
phrases.en: gathering and collecting all the power of his intellect to connect only with this concept.

blocks.text: **But the contraction and squeezing of *ha'amakas hadaas*** is exactly the opposite: **is, on the contrary, only contraction**. Not to go into all the things, but rather the opposite: to contract away all the other things, to focus and gather together the whole power of your brain, **to connect only with this concept**. Like what we're doing now, taking the whole power of our brain. "Why are we focusing our whole brain? There are so many things to think about, and we're thinking only about *daas*." It's exactly the opposite of *bina*.

phrases.he: שזה היפך בחינת התפשטות העיון בהרחבת ענין המושכל,
phrases.en: This is the opposite of the spreading out of *iyun* in widening the concept

phrases.he: (בל"א דער קלעפ מיט דעם אריין לייגין זיך גאר כו')
phrases.en: (in Yiddish: he is stuck to it, laying himself into it altogether);

phrases.he: ואמנם על ידי העמקת הדעת בא לידי עמקות המושכל עד שרשו בעמקי החכמה ובינה
phrases.en: yet through *ha'amakas hadaas* one comes to the depth of the concept, to its root in the depths of *chachma* and *bina*

blocks.text: **This is the opposite of the spreading out of *iyun* in widening the concept**: of analyzing all the different parts. **in Yiddish: he is stuck to it, laying himself into it altogether**: he busies himself only with this thing and nothing else. Like here: we're only busying ourselves with the matter of *daas* and nothing else, totally focusing our brain, gathering the whole power of our brain and putting it only on this, to the exclusion of everything else.

**yet through *ha'amakas hadaas* one comes to the depth of the concept**: *davka* from concentrating on it, when we're learning this point. It's not that we're not going to learn the other points, and we're just going to stay with this, and stay with this forever, and go over and over and over it again.

We'll sit in a cave in the Himalayas and we'll go: "*Daas* is delving, *daas* is the concentration of all the powers of your brain, *daas* is the concentration of all the powers of your brain, *daas*..." That's what they do, basically.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks Eastern meditators in a Himalayan cave repeating a phrase.
sensitivity.publishable: It's not that we'll just sit and repeat: "*Daas* is delving, *daas* is the concentration of all the powers of your brain, *daas* is the concentration of all the powers of your brain, *daas*..."

blocks.text: It's not that we're not going to get to the other points. We're going to get to the other points: the next chapter is going to be about *tevuna*, and then we're going to forget about *daas*, talk about *tevuna*, and concentrate the whole thing *davka* on that. When you're doing a particular point you're totally concentrated on that point, and that is what will bring you to the actual depth of the concept, **to its root in the depths of *chachma* and *bina***, as it is in the depth of *chachma* and *bina*, and, as it said, in *taalumos chachma*.

blocks.text: **up to *daas elyon*, which unites *chachma* with *bina***: that is like the *Keser*, which is above *chachma* and *bina* and puts them both together. When you have the inner connection, that's what they call knowing the thing: you learned it, and now you know it. Knowing means the knowledge, not the *daas tachton* (lower knowledge). The *daas tachton* is a *daas* that's only the *kli*. The *daas elyon* means that the thing is now part of your brain, connected to you, one thing with you, like "Adam knew Chava": they became one thing. So the *daas elyon* means you learned it, and now the whole *chachma* and *bina* is connected together in the *Keser*, which connects *chachma* and *bina*, **as written above about the depth of the concept in *bina***.

**and this is [what is said,] *daas* is hidden in the mouth of *Ima***: the *daas* is hidden inside the mouth of *bina*. The mouth is like *Malchus*, but the upper *Malchus*; so *davka* when you want to say out the *bina*, like what we're doing now, you have to bring the *daas* into it. That's where the *daas* is hidden. Before, we weren't concentrating on this; *davka* now that we want to bring it out, to talk it out, you see the concentration automatically comes into it. We're really not trying to concentrate; we're not doing like the yogis, that we sat down and now we're going to concentrate. We're trying to understand; and not only that, we're trying to have a lesson, we're talking. So automatically you see the *daas* becomes revealed, because that's where it was hidden in the first place.

blocks.text: **and as they said, Moshe, who is *daas***: Moshe is the *daas*, which doesn't mean a *daas* like the *daas* of the goyim. This is a Jewish *daas*, and a Jewish *daas* means it goes *davka* into the *bina*. Whereas the goyishe *daas* is a *daas* of *Tohu*: the whole thing of *Tohu* is that each *sefira* is on its own, not connected to the other *sefiros*. So the goyishe *daas* is not connected to *bina*. It's just *daas*, just concentration. On what? What do you mean, on what? Concentration just all by itself: *Tohu*.

blocks.text: So *davka* Moshe, who is the *daas*, because he was connected to the matter, was the one who **merited *bina*, which is the *shaar hanun***. **for one depends on the other**, *mamash*. As it says: if there's no *daas* there's no *bina*, and if there's no *bina* there's no *daas*. ("I think that's the order, right?") What does it mean? If you don't concentrate on your lesson, you won't understand nothing; and if there's nothing to understand, you're going to lose interest. If there's no *daas tachton* of concentrating on the lesson, there's not going to be no understanding; and if there's no understanding, there won't be the *daas elyon*, and you won't know nothing. If there's just a concentration with no explanation, it won't go from *daas tachton* to *daas elyon*. You'll just sit there and concentrate, and you won't know nothing; and if you do end up knowing something, it'll just be a vain imagination.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is concentration only a *kli*, "an instrument for an instrument", and what goes wrong when it is taken for the thing itself?
What is a *tamtzis*, and what do instant coffee and knowing how to add show about the depth of the concept?
Why are inventions made by the engineers of a field and not by someone meditating in the Himalayas, and what does the Rebbe Rashab's advice on learning Gemara add?
How is the *navon* higher than the wise man, and what did the Wright brothers see in a bicycle chain?
The text says length and width depend on the depth. What is "the real main point of this chapter" going the other way, and what does it mean for how a student learns?
How is the contraction of deep *daas* the opposite of the spreading of *iyun*, and why does each one need the other?
